extraction_scope: Worker-6 bounded mechanism ontology adjudication from source-located figure captions, methods, results, discussion, and recovered supplementary PDF.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: TN6 and D-TN6 were observed computationally to move toward and penetrate a model E. coli membrane during molecular dynamics simulations.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Computational membrane-positioning evidence supports mechanism context but is not treated as direct killing-mechanism proof by itself.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: TPP+ potentiometric measurements support peptide-induced bacterial membrane depolarization; D-TN6 activity began at lower concentration than TN6 in the E. coli DH5α assay and both peptides depolarized S. aureus at reported concentrations.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Depolarization evidence is source-located but remains one mechanism layer alongside microscopy and MIC data.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SEM/TEM images and accompanying source text report membrane/cell-envelope damage in D-TN6-treated E. coli, including pits, blistering, protrusions, and damaged/degenerated cell-wall morphology.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Microscopy supports membrane/cell-envelope disruption; it is not generalized to all tested organisms without direct images.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Proteinase K treatment fragmented TN6 while D-TN6 retained its HPLC retention profile and activity, supporting protease resistance for the D-form peptide.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Protease resistance is a stability property, not a direct antimicrobial killing mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: In vivo wound and infection model results support D-TN6 efficacy context and low-toxicity context at tested conditions, with biochemical and cytokine values available in recovered supplementary Tables S4-S6.
mechanism_claims.limitations: In vivo outcome context is not converted into a direct antimicrobial mechanism claim.
